decisions.reason: The supplier defines a formal removal, not a map; the old definition also incorrectly calls the expansion inclusion a retraction. A collapse map is now explicitly any retraction of the expansion inclusion, with existence and its homotopy-inverse property proved by the characteristic-ball deformation.

Step 1.2 assigns a finite-matrix K1 class to possibly infinite free modules. This extraneous assertion is invalid, although the nilpotent finite-sum inverse and the statement's separately qualified finite-basis K1 conclusion are sound. The proof now imposes finiteness at every K1 assertion.

F1 incorrectly calls the module bases Z-bases: a rank-one module over Z/2 has no abelian-group basis. Replacing this by right R-bases matches both the definition and the calculation; the quotient sentence was also corrected to apply to the signed torsion class.

Clause 1 confuses deck equivariance of the differential with right-linearity of an individual deck transformation. With c*g=T_(g^-1)c, T_h(c*g)=T_h(c)*(hgh^-1), which differs from T_h(c)*g for noncommuting h,g. Replaced the false based-module assertion with the integral-chain and conjugation-semilinear assertions.

The fixed disk boundary in old step 3.1 need not be cellular, so relative cellular approximation on that prism was not licensed. The repair applies approximation to W=L union the actual r-cell, relative to L; its inclusion and approximated endpoint are cellular. Restriction to the characteristic disk then gives exactly the needed r+1 skeleton bound.

Stable normality supplies an elementary factorization only after finite stabilization. Old step 5.1 silently used it at the original size. The repaired proof stabilizes first, performs the slides at that size, and removes the added identity block by explicit homotopy-level free-face cancellations, retaining the original PAQ claim.

The original assertion 4 uses [u_n] although an isomorphism between displayed free modules over a non-IBN ring can have a rectangular matrix. Equal odd/even totals inside each complex do not imply equal degreewise basis sizes between complexes. Added exactly the degreewise square-matrix condition, leaving the arbitrary-ring formulas intact. Also made explicit that F and G themselves have defined torsion, since their names differ from the opening C,D,E.

Step 5.1 incorrectly kills a group element already in reduced K1, whereas only [-1] is killed there. Over Z[t,t^-1], determinant detects [t] modulo signs. Retained the signed [lambda] cone torsion in reduced K1 and applied the Whitehead quotient only at the final step.

The cited expansion proof does establish identity-cone torsion, but its Statement does not export it, and the contract grammar permits only claim-section quotations. Removed that unsupported fact attribution: identity-map torsion follows locally from composition, and the identity-cone calculation is now supplied locally for cellular isomorphisms.

The rejection overlooks the cited supplier's actual proof: its step 2.1 explicitly constructs the collar that replaces a null-homotopic lower attaching map by a constant map and transports upper attachments. The cancellation item first proves the required nullity in step 1.1. This is a reference to an established construction, not an unsupported inference from elementary matrix operations; no item repair is needed.
